narrative: Privileged DBA j.kwon logged into SSO after hours from a BYOD laptop (okta_auth.jsonl:1), then ran three unapproved bulk exports against db-prod-01 — customers, payment_methods, and salaries (db_audit.jsonl:2-4) — totaling ~97,870 sensitive records. Their workstation DBA-WS-03 then uploaded ~30MB to an unsanctioned personal cloud-storage endpoint at 198.51.100.44 (fw_traffic.jsonl:1-3). Blast radius: db-prod-01, the j.kwon identity, and the customers / payment_methods / salaries datasets.
decoy: The scheduled ETL service account svc_etl_nightly exported 500,000 rows of the orders table (db_audit.jsonl:1) — far more volume than the insider. Ranking by row count alone points here, but that job ran during business hours, was approved/whitelisted, and the account is rated benign in threat_intel.csv:1. A correct agent must NOT attribute the theft to the high-volume ETL job and must self-correct to j.kwon's after-hours, unapproved exports.
root_cause: A privileged DBA abused legitimate access for after-hours, unapproved bulk exports of sensitive tables and uploaded them to an unsanctioned personal cloud endpoint.

expected_findings.label: After-hours bulk data export by a privileged user

expected_decoy_rejections.claim: The svc_etl_nightly job (500K rows) is the data-theft culprit because it moved the most data
expected_decoy_rejections.must_reject_because: that export ran during business hours, was approved/whitelisted, and the account is benign (threat_intel.csv:1); volume alone is not exfiltration
